source_spans.locator: Nature Neuroscience 9(11), PDF p.1 / published p.1432, abstract and Results opening: variable population responses encode distributions rather than only point values
Nature Neuroscience 9(11), PDF p.2 / published p.1433, cue-integration derivation: summing two population responses under stated assumptions yields the optimal combined distribution
Nature Neuroscience 9(11), PDF p.3 / published p.1434, generalization: broader Poisson-like families admit optimal linear combinations and realistic-neuron implementation is approximate

conditions: population responses have the declared exponential-family noise structure; simple summation additionally requires matched response profiles and a flat prior
task: combine uncertain cues about an underlying stimulus variable
temporal_scope: single-trial population responses and their combined output

nodes.description: first noisy population response associated with one cue
second noisy population response associated with another cue
probability distribution over the latent stimulus implied by the first population response
probability distribution over the latent stimulus implied by the second population response
addition or weighted linear combination of the input population activities
output population whose activity encodes the cue-combined distribution
distribution width or inverse precision implied by response gain and used to test whether the combined output has the optimal uncertainty

relations.description: the first variable population response specifies a probability distribution over the latent stimulus
the second variable population response specifies another probability distribution over the latent stimulus
the declared linear transform combines the two input activities into an output activity pattern
under the declared noise assumptions the output distribution has the precision required by the optimal cue-combination rule; with realistic nonlinear units this correspondence is tested approximately
